questions.title: Discuss the role and importance of programmed data backup and version control when producing and implementing code. (Q31, ITE 2025)

items.text: Discuss the role and importance of programmed data backup and version control when producing and implementing code.

criteria.criterion: Excellent discussion of the role and importance of programmed backups and the role and importance of version control.
Thorough discussion the role and importance of programmed backups and the role and importance of version control lack of clarity.
Discusses the role and importance of programmed backups OR the role and importance of version control lack of clarity.
Response shows some understanding of backups OR version control.

markingGuidanceContentItem.text:
When producing and implementing code, programmed data backup ensures that project files, databases, and environments are regularly saved and can be recovered in case of accidental loss, system failure, or corruption. Automated backup systems reduce the risk of losing work, especially during major updates or modifications, and are essential for maintaining data integrity throughout the development lifecycle.

On the other hand, version control systems like Git are used to track changes in the codebase, allowing developers to work collaboratively, manage updates, and revert to earlier versions if needed. Version control records the history of changes, making it easier to identify when and where bugs were introduced and to coordinate teamwork across multiple programmers.

During code implementation, combining both tools provides a safety net: version control manages the logical flow and collaboration of coding, while backups protect the broader system—including files not typically tracked in version control, like databases and configuration settings. This ensures recovery is possible even if a deployment error affects the live environment.

questions.title: Define version control. (Q25, ITE 2016)

items.text: Define version control.

criteria.criterion: States meaning AND provides essential qualities of version control.
States meaning OR provides essential qualities of version control.

sampleAnswerContentItem.text: Version control is management of changes to software. As software is updated previous versions are retained in case developers need to roll back to an earlier version. Each new version can be assigned a version number, e.g. version 1, version 1.01 etc.

questions.title: Managing Collaborative Software Development with Version Control (Question 25, ITE 2018)

items.text: A range of issues can arise when multiple developers are working on a single software project. Describe some issues that can occur along with how software version control  systems could assist managing these issues.

criteria.criterion: Describes issues with multiple developers working on the same  source code and provides specific examples of how version control  systems can assist.
Describes some issues with multiple developers working on the  same source code with some reference to version control systems.
Identifies an issue with multiple developers working on the same  source code.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
Answers could include: 

• Conflicts when developers modify the same modules simultaneously. It is  possible that on projects, particularly those involving large teams, that multiple  developers may edit the same source code files at the same time. If a simple  cloud based file storage solution was being used, this could result in one  developers changes overwriting another developer’s changes. Version control  systems manage this situation and can assist in merging multiple changes in the  same modules, at the same time, back into that module without work being lost. 

• Documentation of changes. If many developers are working on a project it can  be difficult to see what changes have been made and by whom. Using a version  control system keeps accountability through a log of who changed what, and  when those changes were made. 

• Rolling back changes. It is possible that updates to source code by someone  else introduced bugs which were not present in previous versions. In the event  of a catastrophic issue, modules or entire sections of the program can be rolled back to previous stable versions. 

• Continuous development. New features and versions may wish to be  developed, but they might be reasonably long-term. In these situations, a version  control system allows for “branching” whereby a new branch of development  can be commenced based upon the current stable release of the software, but  that branches development is separate to the main line of development. This  means new features/versions can be worked on while the current version can be  maintained.

questions.title: Strategies for Locating Code in Software Maintenance (Question 30, ITE 2023)

items.text:
A software company develops an accounting package and releases it to the market. After a year, several updates are required to the software, including changes to taxation rates.

Describe strategies that the maintenance programmers could use to locate the section of the code that has to be changed.

criteria.criterion: Describes strategies for locating the section of code
Describes a strategy OR identifies strategies for location the section of code
Shows some understanding of code maintenance

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
Strategies include:

  • examining developer documentation such as structure charts, IPO diagrams and data dictionaries for relevant terms and variables, such as ‘tax’ or ‘rate’. This will narrow down the subroutine in which the relevant changes need to be made.
  • opening the code in an appropriate code editor and using the find function to search for key terms such as ‘tax’.
  • Given tax rates are likely to change, it is likely they are being loaded from a configuration or setup file. Developer documentation should indicate such files and identify the code that opens relevant files and loads such data.

questions.title: Social and Ethical Issues (Question 25, ITE 2021)

items.text:
Consider the following quote:

Atlassian employees can choose to work wherever they want, whether at home, in an office, or a combination of the two. 

- Business Insider, 8 August 2020

Outline TWO issues for software developers with the recent trend towards working remotely rather than at a corporate office.

criteria.criterion: Outlines TWO issues for software developers when working remotely.
Identifies TWO issues or outlines ONE issue for software developers when working remotely.
Identifies ONE issue for software developers when working remotely.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
• Communication. Software developers often work in teams, and communication amongst the team is very important. With remote work alternative means of communication need to be found and used, such as instant messaging or video conferencing, to ensure that the software team can still effectively communicate with each other.

  • Source control. Control of source code with developers working in multiple different locations can be challenging, so some kind of version control system (such as Git) should be used to manage the source code. This will also need to be accessible outside of the local network of the company to ensure that employees are able to remotely access the source code repositories.

  • Security. The software developers may be working on projects which are confidential or are closed source, so developers need a secure way to access the resources which they need to complete the project. Technologies such as a VPN back to the corporate network can assist with ensuring security of the connection between the remote site and corporate office.

criteria.criterion: Provides some detail on TWO reasons for source code changes
Identifies TWO reasons or provides some detail on ONE reason for source code changes
Identifies ONE reason for source code changes

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
Changes in government requirements. Legal changes can result in software updates, for example if the GST rate was changed then most point of sale software would require updating.

Poorly implemented code. Over time, bugs in the original code may become apparent. Developers need to fix these and release an update to the software.

Answers could also include changing user requirements, UI updates, changes in data to be processed, changes to hardware or the software environment, changing organisational focus.

questions.title: Describe challenges that may be faced when working with a remote contract programmer (Question 25, ITE 2019)

items.text: Describe challenges that may be faced when working with a remote contract programmer.

criteria.criterion: Describing challenges which may be faced working with a remote contract programmer.
Identifies challenges which may be faced working with a remote contract programmer.
Defines a feature of a remote contract programmer.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
Challenges may include:
● Time differences: The remote contract programmer is possibly working in a different time
zone, requiring either the contract programmer or the employer to hold meetings at odd hours
outside of normal working times.
● Communication barriers: The remote contract programmer may not speak the same native
language as the employer - creating communication challenges, particularly in terms of
communicating the software or system requirements to the programmer.
● Software quality: Contract programmers may bit a low fixed-rate amount to secure the job,
but will then produce the minimum work to meet the requirements. As they do not necessarily
have a vested interest in the finished product the quality of their work may be the bare
minimum.
● Monitoring work: If the contract programmer is being paid by the hour then it is important to
keep track of their progress, to ensure that they are completing the set work in a reasonable
timeframe and not incurring unnecessary expense for the employer.

questions.title: Searching and Structuring Aircraft Records Using Arrays of Records (Question 27, ITE 2021)

items.text:
According to Wikipedia, Qantas currently operates a fleet of 126 aircraft. Globally there are hundreds of thousands of aircraft.

A program currently stores information about just the Qantas fleet in an array of records. Three of the records are shown below.
Justify the use of an array of records for the storage of this data during processing

criteria.criterion: Justifies the use of arrays AND records, showing an understanding of storage and the scenario.
Justifies the use of arrays OR records

markingRubricContentItem.text:
Each aircraft is stored in a record with fields registration (string), Airline (string), Delivery Date (date), Name (string) and Type (string). The inclusion of different data types makes a record an appropriate data structure.

The record for each aircraft is then combined into an array of records, where each element of the array is a record with one aircraft. This allows for ease of processing, for example searching or sorting the array.

items.text:
Write a linear search algorithm to return the Delivery Date of an entered aircraft Name. The program should return a suitable error message if the name is not found.

Assume the variable numRecords holds the number of records and that the first record has an array index of 0.

criteria.criterion:
Correct algorithm, including the following features:

  • looping through the array with appropriate bounds

  • addressing of the array of records

  • returning the delivery date if the aircraft is found

  • returning an appropriate error message if the aircraft is not found
Substantially correct algorithm
An algorithm with some correct features
An algorithm showing some understanding of the problem

items.text: Discuss situations and conditions where a binary search is more suitable for searching the array of aircraft.

criteria.criterion: Shows a thorough understanding of binary search and how it applies to this array of records.
Shows some understanding of binary search
Identifies a feature of binary search

markingRubricContentItem.text:
For a binary search to be used, the array needs to be sorted by the field being searched. In the example data, the array is not sorted by Name, so a binary search based on Name is not possible. The array appears to be sorted by registration, so only a binary search for an aircraft with a specific registration is possible. Alternatively, the array could be sorted by the field being searched first, then a binary search is possible. For example, sort the array by the name field before doing a binary search based on aircraft name. 

Considerations for developers include:

  • whether different search fields are needed or whether users are searching based on the same field all the time. If it’s the same field all the time, sort by that field so that binary searches are possible. If it’s different fields, use a linear search, sort first, or consider keeping different copies of the array in memory, where they are sorted by different fields.

  • how often the array of records will be updated. In this example the updates would be very infrequent. In other situations as new records are added they would need to be sorted into order.

  • The number of records should be considered. A binary search is faster but the increase in speed will only become noticeable when the number of records is significant.

questions.title: Generating and Applying Test Data During the Software Development Lifecycle (Q28, CSSA 2014)

items.text: During the development of a complex software solution test data may be generated. Identify the TWO stages in the software development cycle when this might occur and state the purpose of the testing in both of these stages.

criteria.criterion: Identifies two stages and substantially states the purpose for software testing in both
Identifies a stage and the purpose of testing in that stage

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
Test data may be generated during:

    • Plan and design stage: the purpose is to test the logic within algorithms

    • Implementation stage: the purpose would be to provide input data to test the execution i.e. black box testing

    • Testing and Evaluation stage: purpose would be to simulate real live data and to test the successful implementation

    • Test data that is generated during analysis and design stages of the software development cycle. Algorithms are created to determine IPO and ensure the correctness of an algorithm or program

items.text: System level testing ensures that all the components of the final system work together efficiently. Identify THREE components of a system and provide an example of testing for each of these.

criteria.criterion: Identifies three components AND  gives an example for each
Identifies three components OR gives three examples of testing
Identifies only two components or gives three examples of testing
Identifies only one component with an example of testing

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
• System level testing ensures that hardware, software, data, personnel and procedures that form the components of the final system are able to work together efficiently, correctly and in the manner intended with the new software product.  Not only does the software need to operate correctly, it must operate correctly within the various system environments in which it will be implemented

  • Hardware: The software product should be installed and tested on different combinations of hardware ranging from those specified as the minimum requirements to those that include any additional hardware devices

  • Software: Other software installed on the system will have an effect on the operation of new software products

  • Data: The data input into the system is the most likely source of errors. The product needs to be tested with a large combination and quantity of live test data to ensure its reliability under live conditions

  • Personnel and Procedures: The users of the system will have various skill and knowledge levels. Does the product cater effectively to the needs of users of the product?

questions.title: Give an example of how testing at one level can impact testing at another level. (Question 28, ITE 2023)

items.text: The three levels of software testing are module, program, and system. Give an example of how testing at one level can impact testing at another level.

criteria.criterion: The three levels of software testing are module, program, and system. Give an example of how testing at one level can impact testing at another level.
Describes one level of testing with an attempt at an example.
Describes one level of testing

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
Module level testing is concerned with testing software modules or components in isolation to ensure they function correctly. For example, there might be a module in an accounting software package which calculates tax. 

Program level testing is focussed on testing the interaction and integration between components. Following our example, that would be all the different components and modules in the accounting software. If a module does not function correctly it may impact other modules which are reliant on that module, hence errors when performing program level testing will occur. For example, if the payroll module is reliant on the output of the tax calculation module then this may cause the payroll module to produce incorrect results, which in turn results in incorrect results from the program as it is using and trusting the incorrect output of the tax module.

questions.title: Describe the actions you would take to address the issues identified in the above software testing report. (Q30, ITE 2024)

items.text:
Consider the following software testing report:

Software Testing Report

Product Name: XYZ Project Management Application

Version: 1.0.2

Testing Period: 01/05/2024 - 15/05/2024

Test Summary:

- Total test cases executed: 127

- Passed test cases: 115

- Failed test cases: 12

Critical Issues:

1. User authentication fails when passwords contain special characters.

2. Deadlock occurs when multiple users attempt to update the same task simultaneously.

3. Memory leak detected in the reporting module, causing gradual performance degradation.

 

Major Issues:

1. Sort functionality in the task list view is not working as expected.

2. Date format in the calendar view is inconsistent with the system date format.

3. Printing project reports results in misaligned text and truncated content.

 

Minor Issues:

1. Tooltip text for the "Add Task" button is misleading.

2. Incorrect error message displayed when attempting to delete a completed task.

3. Unused code segments found in several source files, increasing the application's file size.

 

Recommendations:

- Prioritize fixing the critical issues, as they pose significant risks to the application's security, stability, and performance.

- Address the major issues promptly, as they impact core functionalities and user experience.

- Resolve minor issues during the next scheduled maintenance release.

- Conduct thorough regression testing after implementing fixes to ensure no new issues are introduced.

- Consider implementing automated testing frameworks to streamline future testing efforts.

 

Prepared by: Mr McTest
Describe the actions you would take to address the issues identified in the above software testing report.

criteria.criterion: Describes the process and actions to be taken in addressing the issues identified in the testing report.
Identifies processes and actions which could be taken to address the issues identified in the testing report.
Identifies an action to take in response to the testing report.

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
• Prioritise issues: categorise the issues based on their severity (critical, major, minor) and impact on the application's functionality, performance, and user experience. Prioritise fixing the critical issues first, as they pose significant risks to the application's security, stability, and performance.

  • Root cause analysis: conduct a thorough root cause analysis for each identified issue, especially critical and major issues. Understand the underlying causes of the issues, whether they are related to design flaws, coding errors, or integration problems.

  • Code review and bug fixing: Initiate a code review process, focusing on the areas where issues were reported. Collaborate with the development team to develop and implement appropriate fixes for the identified bugs and issues, then ensure that all fixes are thoroughly tested and reviewed.

  • Testing and verification: conduct comprehensive testing after implementing fixes to ensure that no new issues are introduced and that existing functionalities are not adversely affected. Verify that the fixed issues meet the specified requirements. Consider involving quality assurance (QA) teams or external testers to provide an unbiased perspective on the fixed issues.

questions.title: Using Documentation and Debugging Techniques to Support Software Maintenance (Q29, CSSA 2014)

items.text: Identify TWO types of documentation that would help in the maintenance stage of development, and explain how these can assist the programmer.

criteria.criterion: Identifies two forms of documentation   AND  explains how both types assists
Identifies two forms of documentation   AND  explains how one type assists
Identifies two forms of documentation   OR explains how one type assists

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
Internal documentation incorporated into the source code such as comments or intrinsic documentation such as meaningful variable and procedures names will make it easier for the programmer to understand exactly what the source code is doing. This makes it easier to determine which parts of the code need modifying to achieve the specified changes.

Systems documentation such as systems flowcharts, structure charts, data dictionaries provide an overview of the system and how the various parts interrelate. This provides the programmer with the information to determine the role played by individual components of the system, so they can better determine which parts need to be modified, and the effects of those modifications on other parts of the system.

items.text: A maintenance programmer discovers that bugs exist in a solution. Describe TWO debugging techniques that may be used to locate and correct the bugs.

criteria.criterion: Describes two software debugging tools
Identifies two debugging tools  OR describes one tool
Identifies a debugging tool

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
The software debugger would be used to determine what is happening as the program code executes, to help the programmer better understand what the code is achieving. In turn, this will help them to understand either how the original code works, or why their modifications do not work as expected.

The use of breakpoints allows the programmer to specify particular points in the program where the execution will temporarily stop, allowing them to view the contents of specified variables at that point, or to change the contents (such as a flag that has been incorrectly set by the code) so that execution can continue normally to test if subsequent modules work as expected.

Single line stepping allows the code to execute one line at a time so that the programmer can see the effect of individual lines of code on any variables and output produced. This may make it possible to see the display of required information that may otherwise have been immediately overwritten by some other command, for example.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
• System. Ensures that all the components of a system (hardware, software, data, personnel and procedures) are able to correctly and effectively work together in the manner intended in the software product or system. This also applies to ensuring all programs in a suite of products function correctly together.
  • Program. Testing the overall program to ensure that all the incorporated subroutines and modules function correctly together so that the program achieves its overall purpose.
  • Module. During development, each subroutine and module is tested as it is created to ensure they are meeting their purpose and producing correct results, which can then be used by other modules in the program.

items.text:
In a buyer rewards scheme, customers accumulate points each time they purchase goods.

There are four levels of rewards: Bronze, Silver, Gold and Platinum, depending upon the number of accumulated points.

The algorithm below is used to calculate the reward level each time a purchase is made.

 

BEGIN Reward Module

Get purchase details

Calculate_Points

Update_Reward_Level

END Reward Module

 

BEGIN Calculate_Points

retrieve previous total_points

IF purchase > $500 THEN

points = purchase – 100

ELSE

points = 100

ENDIF

total_points = total_points + points

END Calculate_Points

 

BEGIN Update_Reward_Level

CASEWHEREe total_points is

< 1000 : reward_level = Bronze

1000 – 2000 : reward_level = Silver

2001 – 4000 : reward_level = Gold

OTHERWISE : reward_level = Platinum

ENDCASE

END Update_Reward_Level
